newsitem.title: INDIA: India 96/97 foodgrains output seen at 197 mln T.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 foodgrains output seen at 197 mln T.

text.p: India's foodgrains production in 1996/97 (July-June) is expected to reach 197 million tonnes compared with 185 million the previous season, a finance ministry statement said on Tuesday.
The statement said the bright outlook was mainly due to this year's rainfall distribution, the best in the past five years.
"The outlook of agricultural production in 1996/97 is excellent with foodgrains output likely to reach 197 million tonnes compared with 185 million tonnes in 1995/96," it said.
Foodgrains output in 1995/96 was down nearly six million tonnes compared to the previous year.
The statement said a substantial three million tonnes drop in wheat output plsu declines in rice and coarse cereals production had contributed to the slump in output.
India's wheat procurement in the 1995/96 season dropped steeply to 8.2 million tonnes compared to 12.3 million in the preceding year.
The agriculture ministry said India's 1996/97 winter rice output was estimated at 71.27 million tonnes, up from 69.69 million tonnes in the previous season.
India harvests two rice crops with the bulk of its production coming from the winter crop. Sowing for the winter crop begins in July and the harvest starts from October.
The ministry estimated the 1996/97 winter foodgrain output at about 103.46 million tonnes, an increase of about six million tonnes over the previous year.
The country had foodgrain stocks of about 22.1 million tonnes as on September 1, 1996.
